name: infant hypotonia overview
title: The floppy infant: stabilize an unstable infant with ABCDE first, confirm low tone with the suspension and pull-to-sit tests, then sort central from peripheral hypotonia by consciousness, development, strength and reflexes; each column gives its causes, investigations, and shared treatment by referral and supportive care

root.title: Floppy infant: UNSTABLE? → ABCDE first
lines: hypotonia = less resistance to PASSIVE stretch · NOT the same as weakness
Dextrose: check glucose, treat hypoglycemia NOW · Expose: injury or bleeding
acute onset: most often INFECTION · always consider non-accidental trauma

groups.title: Stable: confirm LOW TONE, then CENTRAL or PERIPHERAL?
lines: vertical suspension: slips through your hands · horizontal: drapes in a U
pull to sit: big head lag (normal head lag gone by 2-6 months)

head: h
Central hypotonia
most common in NEWBORNS
cause: • AT BIRTH: hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, trisomy 21, Prader-Willi
• infection: sepsis, meningitis, herpes simplex, TORCH
inv: • CT or MRI of the brain

head: h
Peripheral hypotonia
motor neuron · junction · muscle
cause: • junction: congenital myasthenic syndrome, infant botulism
inv: • CREATINE KINASE: ↑ in most muscle disorders

rows: • EARLY referral: pediatric neurology, metabolics, genetics
• physiotherapy · occupational therapy · nutrition · psychology · speech-language pathology
